lane: native-resolution lidar scarp channels (scarplet / Steger / Frangi)
hypothesis: Faults the USGS Quaternary catalogue lacks are, in the GeoDAWN region, faults whose scarps are visible in 1 m lidar but are averaged away at 100 m; therefore a multiscale line/structure-tensor field built on the 1 m-LiDAR-derived scarp descriptors and the slope-detrended elevation should rank off-catalogue fault pixels higher than the geophysical-habitat fields the project family has used, and higher than chance.
mechanism: Frangi multiscale vesselness (both polarities) + Steger sub-pixel line localisation + structure-tensor orientation coherence and dominant strike, at 2-20 pixel scales on the 100 m detrended elevation, fused with 1 m-LiDAR scarp amplitude x coherence and a strike-concordance gate, then masked against flat / very steep cultural ground. Emitted as 37,654 dots at >= 2.82 px separation with every dot within 200 m of the known catalogue deleted.
non_fault_process_that_could_mimic_it: Fluvial terrace risers, alluvial-fan incisement edges, landslide head scarps, and - most importantly on flat ground - road cuts, canal banks and field boundaries all produce lineated 1 m scarps with high Hessian response. The strike-concordance term and the relief/slope cultural mask are the controls; the measured result is that the control is incomplete on basin floors, where the field's gain over chance is -0.003 (4/8 folds).
